F38.quote: The Walter P. Reuther Library, Archives of Labor and Urban Affairs was established as the Labor History Archives at Wayne State University in 1960, with the goal of collecting and preserving original source materials relating to the development of the American labor movement.

F38.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31); the event 1960

F39.locus: A brief history of the Reuther Library
F39.quote: In 1975, the Walter P. Reuther Library was constructed with funds given to Wayne State University by the United Automobile, Aerospace, and Agricultural Implement Workers of America, and through a supplementary grant from the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.
F39.claim: the 1975 building, constructed with funds the UAW gave the university and a supplementary federal grant
F39.lineage: the building and the union's gift
F39.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31); the event 1975

F40.locus: A brief history of the Reuther Library
F40.quote: A later gift from the UAW funded the construction of the library's Leonard Woodcock Wing, completed in 1991.
F40.claim: a later UAW gift funded the Leonard Woodcock Wing, 1991
F40.lineage: the building and the union's gift
F40.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31); the event 1991

F41.locus: A brief history of the Reuther Library
F41.quote: The Reuther Library is the largest labor archives in North America and is home to the collections of numerous unions and labor-related organizations.
F41.claim: the largest labor archives in North America, home to the collections of numerous unions and labor-related organizations
F41.lineage: what it is: the largest labor archives

F42.locus: A brief history of the Reuther Library
F42.quote: Its collection strengths extend to the political and community life of urban and metropolitan Detroit, the civil rights movement in Michigan and nationally, and women's struggles in the workplace.
F42.claim: its strengths extend to Detroit's political and community life, the civil rights movement and women's struggles in the workplace
F42.lineage: Detroit, civil rights and women's workplace struggles

F43.locus: A brief history of the Reuther Library
F43.quote: The Reuther Library is also the home of the Wayne State University Archives, established by the Board of Governors in 1958 in recognition of the importance and permanent value of the University's official files, records, and documents.
F43.claim: home of the Wayne State University Archives, established in 1958 for the university's official files
F43.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31); the event 1958

F44.quote: The collections housed in the Reuther Library are freely open to the public. Appointments are not required; however, it is recommended that patrons traveling from out-of-town contact the Reference Archivist in advance at reutherreference@wayne.edu .
F44.claim: collections freely open to the public; appointments not required; out-of-town patrons advised to contact the Reference Archivist in advance

F45.quote: Monday – Friday 9:30am–noon, 1pm-3:30pm … CLOSED Saturday, Sunday, & all University Holidays … To schedule a research appointment, contact Kristen Chinery
F45.claim: reading room hours, weekdays only; a research appointment, when sought, through Kristen Chinery

F46.quote: The Reuther Library collects and facilitates access to historical documentary evidence in order to inspire academic research, serve the information needs of the community, and build knowledge at Wayne State University. Information about donating collection material is available in the Reuther Library Collection Policy .
F46.claim: its collecting purpose: historical documentary evidence for research, the community and the university; donation governed by a Collection Policy

F47.quote: Before visiting the Reuther Library's Reading Room, patrons are encouraged to search for collection material related to their topic.
F47.claim: patrons are encouraged to search before visiting
